stories.title: Game #2 Preview & Open Thread: Sabres vs Blackhawks
stories.summary:
Byram Will Not Play in Buffalo Return



Unfortunately, there is only one “revenge game” tonight. Former defenseman Bowen Byram will not play for Chicago tonight. Blackhawks coach Jeff Blashill said Byram is tending to a family matter. That means Sabres fans will have to wait for Byram’s first game back at KeyBank Center since Buffalo traded him to Chicago this summer. Jordan Greenway is still expected to be in Chicago’s lineup and will face the Sabres for the first time since the trade. Byram’s absence forces Chicago to reshuffle its defense. Kevin Korchinski and Ethan Del Mastro will both make their season debuts after sitting out the Blackhawks’ first two games. Byram didn’t have the best first game, but I’m sure it will improve. Byram got everything he wanted when he was traded: to be the #1 D-man and a big contract, so “revenge” is a little harsh.



Zellweger Is In



There is no longer much uncertainty surrounding Olen Zellweger, and the Byram replacement will get his first look in the blue and gold. Zellweger will make his Sabres season debut tonight after recovering from the concussion he suffered during the preseason against Columbus. He practiced alongside Owen Power on Friday and is listed with Power on Buffalo’s second defense pair in the NHL’s latest projected lineup. That gives Buffalo another high-end skating and puck-moving option on the back end and changes the look of the defense from Thursday’s loss in Columbus. The NHL’s current projection has Matt Grzelcyk returning to the lineup alongside Louis Crevier; they played together in Chicago last year on the third pair, with Zach “fighting” Metsa listed as a scratch.



Updated Projected Lineups



Buffalo Sabres



Forwards



Josh Norris – Tage Thompson – Josh DoanZach Benson – Noah Östlund – Jack QuinnPeyton Krebs – Konsta Helenius – Ryan McLeodJiri Kulich – Sam Carrick – Beck Malenstyn



Defense

Goaltenders



Ukko-Pekka LuukkonenColten Ellis



Scratched: Tyson Kozak, Justin Danforth, Zach MetsaInjured: Alex Lyon, Conor Timmins, Jason Zucker



Starting goalie: NHL currently lists Luukkonen first in its projected lineup.



Chicago Blackhawks



Forwards



Roman Kantserov – Frank Nazar – Patrick KaneTyler Bertuzzi – Anton Frondell – Teuvo TeravainenRyan Donato – Oliver Moore – Nick LardisCole Smith – Ryan Greene – Jordan Greenway



Defense



Alex Vlasic – Ian ColeWyatt Kaiser – Artyom LevshunovKevin Korchinski – Ethan Del Mastro



Goaltenders



Spencer KnightArvid Söderblom



Scratched: Bowen Byram, Sam RinzelInjured: Connor Bedard, Andrew Mangiapane



Starting goalie: NHL currently lists Knight first in its projected lineup.



Final Thoughts



The Byram storyline has changed, but plenty remains around Buffalo’s home opener. Jordan Greenway returns to KeyBank Center in a Blackhawks sweater, Patrick Kane is back in Buffalo, and Olen Zellweger will make his Sabres debut. 



Chicago is also changing two-thirds of its bottom four on defense after surrendering 11 goals through its first two games. For Buffalo, the task remains the same: take advantage of a struggling team, clean up special teams, and establish control early rather than letting Chicago hang around. Last season’s Atlantic Division banner goes up in the rafters tonight.



Then Buffalo gets back to work.

stories.title: Sabres Cannonballed by Columbus, Fall 6-3
stories.summary:
Can We Get a Do-Over?



Score: Buffalo Sabres 3-6 Columbus Blue JacketsShots: BUF 26-23 COL



Buffalo Sabres Goals: Samuelsson 1st (Ostlund, Power) Quinn 1st (Benson, Ostlund)  Helenius 1st (McLeod, Power)Columbus Blue Jackets Goals: Sillinger 1st (Coyle, Mateychuk) Knies 1st (Coyle, Werenski) Fantilli 1st (Werenski, Knies) Knies 2nd (Andrae, Johnson) Monahan 1st ( Nichushkin, Voronkov) Olivier 1st (Coyle)



“Frustrated Incorporated”



Minus 1: Sammy! Then WHAMMY!



Buffalo got a good chance just seconds into the game when Tage Thompson rang one off the iron. Josh Doan followed that up with a nice pass from Josh Norris, taking the puck right to the net, but Jet Greaves of Columbus made a quality save. The Blue Jackets then put on a strong forecheck but couldn’t get the puck to the net for a shot. Carson Soucy was called for cross-checking Sabres forward Jack Quinn, giving Buffalo’s much-maligned power play its first opportunity of the season.



It didn’t last long.



After fumbling the puck at least twice, TNT was called for hooking, negating the rest of the man advantage. That opened the ice for 4-on-4 play and gave Mattias Samuelsson plenty of room to let one rip. Sammy cashed in with a wicked shot that eluded Greaves. Noah Ostlund and Owen Power picked up the assists on Buffalo’s first goal of the new season.



Ten minutes in, the shots were just 3-2 in favor of the Sabres.



Buffalo picked up its fourth and fifth shots while enjoying some quality zone time, but a Columbus breakout would tie the game. Charlie Coyle tried to split the Sabres defense, which closed in on him, but Coyle made a great play to drop the puck back to an open Cole Sillinger. He fired a snapper past a surprised Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen. The Sabres’ forwards were caught too deep and couldn’t get back to cover the man in the slot.



A little later, Buffalo fumbled the puck in front of its own net with some inopportune passing. Samuelsson had to tie up his man to recover, bringing him down and taking a penalty in the process. Columbus cashed in quickly as Matthew Knies snapped a shot on UPL from about 15 feet out that found the twine. The Jackets had now collected four straight shots and two goals. They added another on their next shot. Adam Fantilli’s long-distance blast had eyes, beating Luukkonen again.



The Sabres’ first-period collapse was painful to watch and incredibly discouraging after scoring first on the road. Buffalo’s new and undermanned defense was certainly not in midseason form, and neither was UPL. The Sabres weren’t aggressive enough defensively, repeatedly backing in instead of challenging the Columbus attack. This was a serious shake-your-head period—one Buffalo desperately needed to put behind it. Would they?



Plus 1: Two on the Board but One Against



A quick turnover to start the period allowed Jack Quinn to bring the game back within one. Buffalo held the puck in at the blue line, where Zach Benson came up with it and quickly dished it to Quinn. Benson then drove to the net, taking a Columbus defender with him. Quinn cut wide, setting himself up for the shot before zipping the puck past Jet Greaves. It was a huge goal to start the middle frame and exactly what the Blue and Gold needed.



Buffalo found some new life after the goal, generating more zone time and pressure. The Sabres would draw a penalty on a strong forecheck as Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen headed to the bench. The whistle eventually blew with the puck rolling in front of Buffalo’s empty net. Mathieu Olivier decided he would break the unwritten rules and fired the puck into the yawning cage, and Sabres defenseman Zach Metsa let him know that wasn’t going to fly, giving him a good shove. The hulking Blue Jackets enforcer then decided to go ham, attacking Metsa and firing away with wild punches. Metsa was clearly overmatched and undersized, but to his credit, Zach hung in there. He absorbed Olivier’s relentless barrage and even managed to sneak in a few shots of his own. Metsa did his best to shield himself from the assault, but where were the refs on that one? A much smaller player was essentially in survival mode against a significantly bigger opponent, and the zebras simply stood back and watched. Way to go, NHL.



Buffalo would receive a five-on-three advantage following the incident, but the Sabres couldn’t cash in. A two-man advantage was the perfect opportunity to tie the game, and good teams find a way to capitalize in those situations. Buffalo didn’t, and it would come back to bite them as Columbus reestablished its two-goal lead. Matthew Knies scored again, giving him three points on the night. The former Toronto Maple Leaf seemed possessed, apparently determined to continue finding success against Buffalo even after leaving the Atlantic Division.



The Sabres would get their fourth power play of the night shortly afterward, but once again failed to score. However, Buffalo continued to keep the pressure on and finally found twine moments after the penalty expired. Konsta Helenius scored his first goal of the season after receiving a beautiful cross-ice pass from Ryan McLeod. Owen Power picked up his second assist of the game on the play as well.



The Sabres generated some good zone time for the remainder of the period, but couldn’t find the equalizer. After 40 minutes, Columbus still held a 4-3 lead.







Minus 2: Sammy’s Double Whammy



Buffalo continued to get some zone time early in the period, generating a few chances while pressing the attack. Benson and Ostlund were standouts among the forward ranks. Luukkonen then came up with his best save of the game, getting a piece of the puck while sliding across the crease to deny a Columbus 2-on-1. He had faced just 16 shots to that point, but four of them had already found the back of the net. He remained focused though.



Owen Power then had his stick slashed in half as Sillenger was sent off the ice. Another chance for the dreaded Buffalo power play. Once again, failure, though the Sabres came close with a shot off the post with 3 seconds left. Columbus was all over the puck carrier and was winning most of the face offs. UPL then came up big again, denying Knies of a hat trick on a breakaway. It wasn’t his best outing for sure but he kept his team in it for much of the third period.



Samuelsson then took his second penalty of the evening, this time for tripping. The Sabres nearly killed it off, but Sean Monahan tipped the puck past UPL with just two seconds remaining on the man advantage. Just like that, Columbus had a 5-3 lead. Both of Sammy’s penalties ultimately resulted in Blue Jackets power-play goals.



Buffalo eventually pulled UPL, and, well, we all know how that usually goes. You have a better chance of hitting the Lotto than the Sabres cashing in on a 6-on-5 advantage. After several more puck fumbles, Mathieu Olivier found the empty net to seal a 6-3 Columbus victory. As discussed before the game, the Sabres simply do not match up well against Columbus, for whatever reason. It was a disappointing way to start the new year, with mental mistakes and poor puck control plaguing Buffalo throughout the night. The defense also failed to attack the way it needed to, allowing the Blue Jackets far too much room to operate.



Overall, it was a frustrating game to watch. The Sabres have plenty of work to do and will need to clean up several problem areas before they take the ice again. What a ginormous disappointment. We waited all summer for THAT???



Final Thoughts:



Once again, special teams were a major issue in this game. The power play went 0-for-5, while the penalty kill managed to go just 1-for-3. There’s your game right there. Those are simply dreadful numbers, and the struggles on the faceoff dot only made matters worse. Draws have been an issue with this group for some time, and tonight was no different. Buffalo won just 41 percent of tonight’s faceoffs, including losing many while on the man advantage.



Rasmus Dahlin and Tage Thompson were very quiet in this game, not a good winning recipe.



The Sabres now turn their attention to the Chicago Blackhawks for their home opener on Saturday, October 3rd, at 7 p.m. at KeyBank Center. Former Buffalo defenseman Bo Byram will make his first return to the building.

stories.title: Game #1 Preview & Open Thread: Sabres at Blue Jackets
stories.summary:
Buffalo looking to start off new season on the right foot



Buffalo Sabres (0-0-0) vs Columbus Blue Jackets (0-0-0)



Puck Drop: 7:00 pm ET | Nationwide Arena, Columbus OH



TV: CBJNHL, CBJHN, MSG-B, DAZN, ESPN+, Fubo, Hulu + Live TV



Radio: WGR 550, Sirius XM (app)



Know Your Opponent



Columbus Blue Jackets



Record: 0-0-0 | 0 PTS (40-30-12 for 92pts) /last season



Last Game: N/A



Division Ranking: N/A



PP: 22nd, 18.9% (38/201) [Sabres: 21st, 19.5% (48/246)] /last season



PK: 28th, 76.0% (150/190) [Sabres: 5th, 82.8% (144/174)] /last season



Season Series: Sabres 1-1-1 Blue Jackets /last season



What to Watch



1. Sky-high Expectations



“With a rebel yell, more, more, more. More, more, more!”



With the playoff drought monkey finally off the Sabres’ backs, you would have thought that the Sabrehood would be somewhat sated. Instead, one would say expectations are absolutely sky-high going into tonight’s game. The fans are ready for a Cup-run and last season’s eventual elimination was just a blip in that timeline. 



The Sabres are going to be hard-pressed to repeat that ridiculous late-season run – they went 29-9-5 from when the calendar turned to 2026, the best record in the league with only Stanley Cup champions Carolina Hurricanes one point behind them and everyone else chasing their dust.   



2. Maintain The Level



Buffalo has gotten to their division-winning berth last season by playing high intensity hockey, and they will have to quickly find those levels this season too. The Sabres didn’t make any marquee additions over the offseason, and lost core players Alex Tuch and Bowen Byram. It looks like Olen Zellweger is being touted as the Byram replacement, but otherwise the expectation is that youngsters on the team are going to all make a respective step up.  



Even more importantly, can the three-headed goalie monster replicate their incredible form from last season? Their .899 combined save percentage was second in the league and carried them to the playoffs.



3. A Pesky Opponent



Columbus have been a bit of a bogey team for the Sabres for some time now, their hard-hitting physical game has frustrated the Sabres often enough over the last few seasons with Buffalo 6-7-2 in the last five years. The Blue Jackets traded away Kirill Marchenko and Elvis Merzlikins and added Matthew Knies, and will have to decide who they really are as they seek a new identity. 



Led by star defenseman Zach Werenski and young center Adam Fantilli and boosted by veterans Charlie Coyle, Sean Monahan and Valeri Nichushkin with another young playmaker in Kent Johnson, there’s still lots of talent in this side. Goalie Jet Greaves will be looking to make an impression too, this is a dangerous opponent.

stories.title: Buffalo Sabres sign defenseman Louis Crevier to four-year extension
stories.summary:
Even before he has played his first game for the Buffalo Sabres tonight, Louis Crevier has decided he wants to stick around, signing a four-year contract extension worth $16 million ($4M AAV). 



The 6’8″ defenseman had signed a two-year, $1.8 million contract with the Chicago Blackhawks on July 17, 2025, before being traded to the Buffalo Sabres in June 2026, and this extension marks a big raise for the hulking player. The Sabres now have five defensemen signed through the end of the 2028-29 season, which is a sign of stability at the position. 




The Buffalo Sabres have signed defenseman Louis Crevier to a four-year extension with an AAV of $4 million. pic.twitter.com/n57zNRKcu3— Buffalo Sabres PR (@SabresPR) October 1, 2026




Crevier joined the Sabres as part of the return for star defenseman Bowen Byram who went to the Windy City. The 25-year-old dman has featured in 134 career NHL games after getting drafted 188th overall by the Blackhawks in the 2020 NHL Draft. He has scored 10 goals with 22 assists, and was ranked second in Chicago last season in a couple of key defensive metrics with 95 blocked shots and 124 hits.



Lindy Ruff is happy with what he has seen so far in practice and in the preseason games – 



“When I’ve watched him at practice, we’ve had lots of discussions about him. We’ve watched him in the games, he’s moved the puck well and skated well. There was a little concern coming off [shoulder] surgery this summer, but everything looks great. I think this will be a great fit for our hockey club.”



Crevier for his part just wanted to settle his future before the season started – 



“I’m really happy. It’s something I’ve worked at for awhile now, and I’m just super glad it’s behind me. Just having stability, I think will help me a ton to play hockey. 



“Everyone was really welcoming, and since it happened in the summer, I was free to process more-and-more information, learn names and stuff, even before I came into Buffalo. I think that helped a lot. It was just super easy, honestly.”



About his fellow blue-liners, the dman was very complimentary – 



“I think they’re all really good players, so it helps a lot. In Chicago, it was the same even earlier in the year last year. We were playing seven defensemen, so I feel like I’m used to playing with different guys.”



Crevier has been the most successful seventh rounder so far from that 2020 draft with 134 games played, with Ilya Solovyov of the Pittsburgh Penguins behind him at 45 games and a guy who featured in the Rochester local news shoveling his sidewalk (Devon Levi) in third with 39 games played.

stories.title: Letter from Levi Wallace talking about what he went through to play football throughout the years
stories.summary:
Kind of a neat article for those of you who subscribe to the Athletic.  It's a letter written by Levi Wallace's mind to his body, kind of apologizing to his body for the things he put his body through to play football.  Below is the first and last couple of paragraphs, starts out from when he first played flag football at age 5 up until he decided to retire. 



	 



	Article was called "Here's the truth from a retiring NFL player"



	 



	Dear Body,



	The time has finally come for me to acknowledge that we are in agreement. It is time for us to call it quits.



	 



	I owe you a letter that tells the truth. Not the highlight version. The real one. The version where people saw us on Sundays but never saw what it took to get there.



	 



	..........



	 



	 



	Somewhere along the way, we learned how to carry each other, Body and Mind.



	 



	Truth be told, Body, I wouldn’t change a thing. I’d put us through it all over again. Because I know what we are capable of.



	 



	I know what God built us to endure.



	 



	I know we can handle it together.



	 



	Sincerely,



	Levi Wallace’s Mind

The Sabres are coming off an impressive but costly win over Columbus on Tuesday night at KeyBank Center. The team lost two defensemen in Mattias Samuelsson and newcomer Olen Zellweger.



Samuelsson suffered a lower-body injury, likely while blocking a shot, and his prognosis is week-to-week. That’s certainly not what you want to see with the official first puck drop of the season right around the corner. Rasmus Dahlin’s defensive partner will now be out for at least a handful of games, maybe more.



To add insult to yet another injury, Zellweger will miss at least a week, and potentially longer, with a concussion. Olen was having himself a nice preseason game until he was leveled by a “regular-season” type of hit in the second period while setting up a teammate.



Well wishes to both players. Hopefully, Mattias and Olen will be back in the lineup sooner rather than later. Buffalo’s defensive depth looks like it will be tested early to start the season now. Let’s just hope the team can skate away from the final two preseason tilts without any further damage.



The Sabres will ice a much less potent lineup tonight against Detroit, with most of their expected roster players sitting this one out. Konsta Helenius and Noah Ostlund will be in the lineup for Buffalo, though, along with Jiri Kulich again. So at least fans will get to see some of our young guns in action tonight.

stories.title: DBTB makes three free agent additions!
stories.summary:
After an incredible season for the Buffalo Sabres that saw them end a long-suffering playoff drought and come oh-so-close to a Conference Final berth, Die By The Blade has made some moves to beef up the roster going into the new season. 



First a big thank you to Steven Staversky who leaves DBTB to tend to his growing family. He helped us keep the site running at some of the darker times in Sabres history and we appreciate his efforts, and wish him well. 



Let’s jump into the bios of the three new writers joining the DBTB team. 



HickeyHockey



In little Buffalo, Roc City. Bleed blue, gold, red and black but the other 33 teams are alright. I coach, Fantasy and drive a Zamboni, so I can cover all areas.







Adam1439



I’m a WNY native that’s followed the Sabres my entire life. The teams of the mid-2000s are some of my favorite, early sports memories, and that childhood fandom (for better or worse) kept me hooked during the drought. My love for hockey and all sports pushed me to eventually pursue a career in journalism. I’ve covered high school, college and professional sports for a variety of publications, including WIVB News 4, where I worked as a full-time digital journalist right after college for two years. 



When I’m not watching the Sabres/Bills, I love hiking, traveling and trying out restaurants around WNY. I’m also a massive soccer fan and play regularly. However, as a devout Tottenham Hotspur supporter, I often question why I even follow the sport.







adolce95



In May of 2007, on a bus back from a school trip, I had my first experience with Sabres hockey and really sports in general. While that game was the overtime loss to Ottawa to end the 06-07 season, 12-year-old me was absolutely enamored by the investment my classmates had in the game. I have been hooked on sports, specifically hockey and baseball, ever since. I attended SUNY Oswego, where I studied broadcasting, even doing radio play-by-play for the Men’s hockey team for two seasons during my junior and senior year. I have covered a variety of high school sports on the airwaves for WDOE and in print at the Dunkirk Observer in Chautauqua County. 



Outside of the Sabres, I am a diehard Mets, Bills, and Michigan State basketball fan (this is because Ryan Miller went there). When I’m not watching sports, I am probably re-playing a Pokemon game, playing Magic the Gathering or Dungeons and Dragons, or laying on the couch, watching a movie with my wife, our two cats, and dog.







The rest of the team remains the same – Jedi and Calvin are still here, with Chad and Eddie overseeing the operations. 



Thank you for sticking with us over the years, please welcome the new writers and here’s looking forward to a great new season!
